document.title: Afghanistan: Bio-Data on Maulawi Abdul Wahab, Taliban Embassy Official in Saudi Arabia (Islama 09278)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Taliban Biography: The Structure and Leadership of the Taliban 1996-2002
document.note: [Confidential] Background on the new Taliban representative in Riyadh. His predecessor Maulawi Dilawar was told to leave Saudi Arabia in September 1998 because of the dispute over Usama bin Ladin. Excised.

persons.name: Maulawi Abdul Wahab
persons.role: Taliban embassy official in Riyadh (first secretary, styling himself charge d'affaires); formerly Taliban representative to the UN in New York since early 1998

mentions.quote: PARA TWO CONTAINS BIO-DATA ON TALIBAN EMBOFF OFFICIAL IN RIYADH MAULAWI ABDUL WAHAB.
HE IS FROM NANGARHAR PROVINCE IN THE EAST AND IS CLOSE TO RESISTANCE LEADER YUNIS KHALIS

persons.name: Maulawi Dilawar
persons.role: Former Taliban charge d'affaires in Saudi Arabia; reportedly later Taliban consul general in Karachi
persons.status_detail: Told to leave Saudi Arabia in September 1998; reportedly Taliban consul general in Karachi

mentions.quote: DEPARTURE OF MAULAWI DILAWAR, THE FORMER TALIBAN "CHARGE" TO SAUDI ARABIA, WHO WAS TOLD TO LEAVE THE COUNTRY IN SEPTEMBER
REPORTEDLY IS NOW TALIBAN CONSUL GENERAL IN KARACHI
LIKE (ABDUL HAKIM) MUJAHID (THE CURRENT TALIBAN REPRESENTATIVE AT THE UN), WAHAB IS NOT A MEMBER OF THE KANDAHARI STREAM
CLOSE TO RESISTANCE LEADER YUNIS KHALIS, FOR WHOM HE WORKED IN PESHAWAR DURING THE 1980'S

persons.name: Usama bin Ladin
persons.role: Terrorist; subject of dispute between Saudi government and Taliban

mentions.quote: DISPUTE WITH THE SAUDI GOVERNMENT OVER THE ISSUE OF TERRORIST USAMA BIN LADIN

persons.name: Alan Eastham
persons.role: US Charge d'Affaires, Islamabad (classifier/signatory of cable)

mentions.quote: CLASSIFIED BY CHARGE D'AFFAIRES ALAN EASTHAM.

events.description: Wahab told the acting POLCOUNS he was unhappy in New York because his family could not settle in
Maulawi Dilawar told to leave Saudi Arabia over dispute about Usama bin Ladin
US Embassy Islamabad cable sending Wahab bio-data to State and Riyadh
Wahab became Taliban representative to the UN in New York.
Wahab told the US Embassy acting political counselor he was unhappy in New York.
Wahab was assigned to go to Riyadh as first secretary of the Afghan Embassy.
Saudi Arabia told Taliban charge Maulawi Dilawar to leave over the dispute concerning Usama bin Ladin.
US Embassy Islamabad cable sent with Wahab's bio-data in response to Riyadh's request.

key_claims: Wahab is not a Taliban insider, so his information is probably not definitive on Taliban positions.
Wahab refers to himself as charge d'affaires of the Afghan Embassy in Riyadh after Dilawar's departure.
Saudi Arabia expelled Taliban charge Dilawar in September 1998 over the Usama bin Ladin dispute.
Wahab and Mujahid are non-Kandahari Taliban from outside the dominant Kandahari stream.
